entries.note: The proposition changes guardrails that “will take years to perfect” into guardrails that “may” take years. The broader retrospective prediction is explicitly tentative.

entries.test: Public tests of the February 2023 ChatGPT showing whether toxic outputs remained systematically accessible despite its apparent safeguards would test this claim.
entries.note: In context, the illusion concerns reliable control of toxic output, not the absence of any improvement.
There is no shared test for possessing understanding or moral views, as distinct from producing behavior consistent with them.
The metaphor expresses contempt without specifying an independently testable standard.

entries.test: Public architectural descriptions and mechanistic experiments could establish whether ChatGPT relies exclusively on superficial word-sequence similarity or uses additional computational representations and processes.
entries.note: “Operates on” weakens the original assertion that superficial similarity is all that matters. The exclusive mechanism claim supplies a testable empirical commitment.

entries.test: Controlled prompt experiments and public research on training-data influence could test whether wording and corpus matching produce the claimed shifts in ChatGPT's apparent political stance.
entries.note: Output variation alone would not establish the proposed causal mechanism.
This is a recommendation about trust.

entries.test: Publicly documented, reproducible jailbreaks of the February 2023 ChatGPT could establish whether harmful outputs remained accessible through its guardrails.
entries.note: The surrounding experiments give the metaphor a concrete meaning: safeguards could be bypassed to obtain harmful outputs.

entries.test: Public technical accounts and controlled robustness experiments could test whether the guardrails depended on superficial cues that could be bypassed while preserving the request's violent meaning.
entries.note: “More easily tricked” becomes the stronger absolute “easily tricked.” The proposition also broadens the denial of conceptual understanding beyond the specific prohibition on recommending violence.

entries.test: Dated patch records, retests of the disclosed anomaly, and subsequent jailbreak reports could establish whether OpenAI fixed it and other vulnerabilities soon emerged through superficial fixes.
entries.note: The disclosure condition is satisfied by publication. The drafter's separate condition incorrectly makes discovery of other vulnerabilities depend on patching this one.

entries.test: Public demonstrations from February 2023 could establish whether ChatGPT still supported multiple harmful uses after its first two months of remediation.
entries.note: “Can” describes an existing capability, not an uncertain future possibility. The harmful-use assertion provides a concrete test despite the characterization “amoral.”

entries.test: Public investigations documenting language-model use in large-scale misinformation campaigns would establish whether the predicted misuse occurred.
entries.note: By the evaluation date, public reporting on actual language-model misinformation operations provides evidence for assessing this forecast.

entries.test: Public technical disclosures and comparative safety experiments could establish whether RLHF alone reduced toxicity and deceit, while archived OpenAI publications would establish what implementation details it disclosed.
entries.note: The central assertion assigns an exclusive causal role to RLHF. The proposition drops deceitfulness and changes preventing additional toxicity into limiting toxicity generally.

entries.test: OpenAI's publicly available datasets and documentation as of February 11, 2023 would establish whether it disclosed the data used for ChatGPT's RLHF.
entries.note: The reference is to the human-feedback training data discussed immediately beforehand.
Neither “fully understand” nor alignment “with ourselves” has a shared success criterion here. The indefinite horizon alone is not the obstacle.

entries.test: Laws, regulations, and enforcement powers in force on February 11, 2023 could establish the extent of government regulation addressing the chatbot harms discussed.
entries.note: The claim concerns regulation at publication, not regulation at the evaluation date.
“Endless possibilities” is hyperbole about opportunities already available, not a firm prediction that specified outcomes will occur.
“Disaster in the making” supplies no distinct outcome or threshold to test.
